verses: 1 1 1 in the beginning god created the heavens and the earth
1 1 2 the earth was formless and empty darkness was on the surface of the deep and god s spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters
1 1 3 god said let there be light and there was light
1 1 4 god saw the light and saw that it was good god divided the light from the darkness
1 1 5 god called the light day and the darkness he called night there was evening and there was morning the first day
1 1 6 god said let there be an expanse in the middle of the waters and let it divide the waters from the waters
1 1 7 god made the expanse and divided the waters which were under the expanse from the waters which were above the expanse and it was so
1 1 8 god called the expanse sky there was evening and there was morning a second day
1 1 9 god said let the waters under the sky be gathered together to one place and let the dry land appear and it was so
1 1 10 god called the dry land earth and the gathering together of the waters he called seas god saw that it was good
1 1 11 god said let the earth yield grass herbs yielding seeds and fruit trees bearing fruit after their kind with their seeds in it on the earth and it was so
1 1 12 the earth yielded grass herbs yielding seed after their kind and trees bearing fruit with their seeds in it after their kind and god saw that it was good
1 1 13 there was evening and there was morning a third day
1 1 14 god said let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night and let them be for signs to mark seasons days and years
1 1 15 and let them be for lights in the expanse of the sky to give light on the earth and it was so
1 1 16 god made the two great lights the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night he also made the stars
1 1 17 god set them in the expanse of the sky to give light to the earth
1 1 18 and to rule over the day and over the night and to divide the light from the darkness god saw that it was good
1 1 19 there was evening and there was morning a fourth day
1 1 20 god said let the waters abound with living creatures and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky
1 1 21 god created the large sea creatures and every living creature that moves with which the waters swarmed after their kind and every winged bird after its kind god saw that it was good
1 1 22 god blessed them saying be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas and let birds multiply on the earth
1 1 23 there was evening and there was morning a fifth day
1 1 24 god said let the earth produce living creatures after their kind livestock creeping things and animals of the earth after their kind and it was so
1 1 25 god made the animals of the earth after their kind and the livestock after their kind and everything that creeps on the ground after its kind god saw that it was good

1 1 26 god said let us make man in our image after our likeness and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the sky and over the livestock and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth
1 1 27 god created man in his own image in god s image he created him male and female he created them

1 1 28 god blessed them god said to them be fruitful multiply fill the earth and subdue it have dominion over the fish of the sea over the birds of the sky and over every living thing that moves on the earth
1 1 29 god said behold i have given you every herb yielding seed which is on the surface of all the earth and every tree which bears fruit yielding seed it will be your food
1 1 30 to every animal of the earth and to every bird of the sky and to everything that creeps on the earth in which there is life i have given every green herb for food and it was so
1 1 31 god saw everything that he had made and behold it was very good there was evening and there was morning a sixth day
1 2 1 the heavens the earth and all their vast array were finished
1 2 2 on the seventh day god finished his work which he had done and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done
1 2 3 god blessed the seventh day and made it holy because he rested in it from all his work of creation which he had done
1 2 4 this is the history of the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created in the day that yahweh god made the earth and the heavens
1 2 5 no plant of the field was yet in the earth and no herb of the field had yet sprung up for yahweh god had not caused it to rain on the earth there was not a man to till the ground
1 2 6 but a mist went up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground
1 2 7 yahweh god formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life and man became a living soul
1 2 8 yahweh god planted a garden eastward in eden and there he put the man whom he had formed

1 2 9 out of the ground yahweh god made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight and good for food including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
1 2 10 a river went out of eden to water the garden and from there it was parted and became the source of four rivers
1 2 11 the name of the first is pishon it flows through the whole land of havilah where there is gold
1 2 12 and the gold of that land is good bdellium and onyx stone are also there
1 2 13 the name of the second river is gihon it is the same river that flows through the whole land of cush
1 2 14 the name of the third river is hiddekel this is the one which flows in front of assyria the fourth river is the euphrates
1 2 15 yahweh god took the man and put him into the garden of eden to cultivate and keep it
1 2 16 yahweh god commanded the man saying you may freely eat of every tree of the garden
1 2 17 but you shall not eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil for in the day that you eat of it you will surely die
1 2 18 yahweh god said it is not good for the man to be alone i will make him a helper comparable to him

1 2 19 out of the ground yahweh god formed every animal of the field and every bird of the sky and brought them to the man to see what he would call them whatever the man called every living creature became its name
1 2 20 the man gave names to all livestock and to the birds of the sky and to every animal of the field but for man there was not found a helper comparable to him
1 2 21 yahweh god caused the man to fall into a deep sleep as the man slept he took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in its place
1 2 22 yahweh god made a woman from the rib which he had taken from the man and brought her to the man
1 2 23 the man said this is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh she will be called woman because she was taken out of man
1 2 24 therefore a man will leave his father and his mother and will join with his wife and they will be one flesh
1 2 25 the man and his wife were both naked and they were not ashamed
1 3 1 now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which yahweh god had made he said to the woman has god really said you shall not eat of any tree of the garden
1 3 2 the woman said to the serpent we may eat fruit from the trees of the garden
1 3 3 but not the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the garden god has said you shall not eat of it you shall not touch it lest you die
1 3 4 the serpent said to the woman you won t surely die
1 3 5 for god knows that in the day you eat it your eyes will be opened and you will be like god knowing good and evil

1 3 6 when the woman saw that the tree was good for food and that it was a delight to the eyes and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise she took some of its fruit and ate and she gave some to her husband with her and he ate it too
1 3 7 their eyes were opened and they both knew that they were naked they sewed fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves
1 3 8 they heard yahweh god s voice walking in the garden in the cool of the day and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of yahweh god among the trees of the garden
1 3 9 yahweh god called to the man and said to him where are you
1 3 10 the man said i heard your voice in the garden and i was afraid because i was naked and i hid myself
1 3 11 god said who told you that you were naked have you eaten from the tree that i commanded you not to eat from
1 3 12 the man said the woman whom you gave to be with me she gave me fruit from the tree and i ate it
1 3 13 yahweh god said to the woman what have you done the woman said the serpent deceived me and i ate

1 3 14 yahweh god said to the serpent because you have done this you are cursed above all livestock and above every animal of the field you shall go on your belly and you shall eat dust all the days of your life
1 3 15 i will put hostility between you and the woman and between your offspring and her offspring he will bruise your head and you will bruise his heel
1 3 16 to the woman he said i will greatly multiply your pain in childbirth in pain you will bear children your desire will be for your husband and he will rule over you

1 3 17 to adam he said because you have listened to your wife s voice and ate from the tree about which i commanded you saying you shall not eat of it the ground is cursed for your sake you will eat from it with much labor all the days of your life
1 3 18 it will yield thorns and thistles to you and you will eat the herb of the field
1 3 19 by the sweat of your face will you eat bread until you return to the ground for out of it you were taken for you are dust and to dust you shall return
1 3 20 the man called his wife eve because she would be the mother of all the living
1 3 21 yahweh god made coats of animal skins for adam and for his wife and clothed them
1 3 22 yahweh god said behold the man has become like one of us knowing good and evil now lest he reach out his hand and also take of the tree of life and eat and live forever
1 3 23 therefore yahweh god sent him out from the garden of eden to till the ground from which he was taken
1 3 24 so he drove out the man and he placed cherubim at the east of the garden of eden and a flaming sword which turned every way to guard the way to the tree of life
1 4 1 the man knew eve his wife she conceived and gave birth to cain and said i have gotten a man with yahweh s help
1 4 2 again she gave birth to cain s brother abel abel was a keeper of sheep but cain was a tiller of the ground
1 4 3 as time passed cain brought an offering to yahweh from the fruit of the ground
1 4 4 abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of its fat yahweh respected abel and his offering
1 4 5 but he didn t respect cain and his offering cain was very angry and the expression on his face fell
1 4 6 yahweh said to cain why are you angry why has the expression of your face fallen
1 4 7 if you do well won t it be lifted up if you don t do well sin crouches at the door its desire is for you but you are to rule over it
1 4 8 cain said to abel his brother let s go into the field while they were in the field cain rose up against abel his brother and killed him
1 4 9 yahweh said to cain where is abel your brother he said i don t know am i my brother s keeper
1 4 10 yahweh said what have you done the voice of your brother s blood cries to me from the ground
1 4 11 now you are cursed because of the ground which has opened its mouth to receive your brother s blood from your hand
1 4 12 from now on when you till the ground it won t yield its strength to you you will be a fugitive and a wanderer in the earth
1 4 13 cain said to yahweh my punishment is greater than i can bear
1 4 14 behold you have driven me out today from the surface of the ground i will be hidden from your face and i will be a fugitive and a wanderer in the earth whoever finds me will kill me
1 4 15 yahweh said to him therefore whoever slays cain vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold yahweh appointed a sign for cain so that anyone finding him would not strike him
1 4 16 cain left yahweh s presence and lived in the land of nod east of eden
1 4 17 cain knew his wife she conceived and gave birth to enoch he built a city and called the name of the city after the name of his son enoch
1 4 18 to enoch was born irad irad became the father of mehujael mehujael became the father of methushael methushael became the father of lamech
1 4 19 lamech took two wives the name of the first one was adah and the name of the second one was zillah
1 4 20 adah gave birth to jabal who was the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock
1 4 21 his brother s name was jubal who was the father of all who handle the harp and pipe
1 4 22 zillah also gave birth to tubal cain the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron tubal cain s sister was naamah
1 4 23 lamech said to his wives adah and zillah hear my voice you wives of lamech listen to my speech for i have slain a man for wounding me a young man for bruising me
1 4 24 if cain will be avenged seven times truly lamech seventy seven times
1 4 25 adam knew his wife again she gave birth to a son and named him seth saying for god has given me another child instead of abel for cain killed him
1 4 26 a son was also born to seth and he named him enosh at that time men began to call on yahweh s name
1 5 1 this is the book of the generations of adam in the day that god created man he made him in god s likeness
1 5 2 he created them male and female and blessed them on the day they were created he named them adam
1 5 3 adam lived one hundred thirty years and became the father of a son in his own likeness after his image and named him seth
1 5 4 the days of adam after he became the father of seth were eight hundred years and he became the father of other sons and daughters
1 5 5 all the days that adam lived were nine hundred thirty years then he died
1 5 6 seth lived one hundred five years then became the father of enosh
1 5 7 seth lived after he became the father of enosh eight hundred seven years and became the father of other sons and daughters
1 5 8 all of the days of seth were nine hundred twelve years then he died
1 5 9 enosh lived ninety years and became the father of kenan
1 5 10 enosh lived after he became the father of kenan eight hundred fifteen years and became the father of other sons and daughters
1 5 11 all of the days of enosh were nine hundred five years then he died
1 5 12 kenan lived seventy years then became the father of mahalalel
1 5 13 kenan lived after he became the father of mahalalel eight hundred forty years and became the father of other sons and daughters
1 5 14 and all of the days of kenan were nine hundred ten years then he died
1 5 15 mahalalel lived sixty five years then became the father of jared
1 5 16 mahalalel lived after he became the father of jared eight hundred thirty years and became the father of other sons and daughters
1 5 17 all of the days of mahalalel were eight hundred ninety five years then he died
1 5 18 jared lived one hundred sixty two years then became the father of enoch
1 5 19 jared lived after he became the father of enoch eight hundred years and became the father of other sons and daughters
1 5 20 all of the days of jared were nine hundred sixty two years then he died
1 5 21 enoch lived sixty five years then became the father of methuselah
1 5 22 after methuselah s birth enoch walked with god for three hundred years and became the father of more sons and daughters
1 5 23 all the days of enoch were three hundred sixty five years
1 5 24 enoch walked with god and he was not found for god took him
1 5 25 methuselah lived one hundred eighty seven years then became the father of lamech
1 5 26 methuselah lived after he became the father of lamech seven hundred eighty two years and became the father of other sons and daughters
1 5 27 all the days of methuselah were nine hundred sixty nine years then he died
1 5 28 lamech lived one hundred eighty two years then became the father of a son
1 5 29 he named him noah saying this one will comfort us in our work and in the toil of our hands caused by the ground which yahweh has cursed
1 5 30 lamech lived after he became the father of noah five hundred ninety five years and became the father of other sons and daughters
1 5 31 all the days of lamech were seven hundred seventy seven years then he died
1 5 32 noah was five hundred years old then noah became the father of shem ham and japheth
1 6 1 when men began to multiply on the surface of the ground and daughters were born to them
1 6 2 god s sons saw that men s daughters were beautiful and they took any that they wanted for themselves as wives
1 6 3 yahweh said my spirit will not strive with man forever because he also is flesh so his days will be one hundred twenty years
1 6 4 the nephilim were in the earth in those days and also after that when god s sons came in to men s daughters and had children with them those were the mighty men who were of old men of renown
1 6 5 yahweh saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth and that every imagination of the thoughts of man s heart was continually only evil
1 6 6 yahweh was sorry that he had made man on the earth and it grieved him in his heart
1 6 7 yahweh said i will destroy man whom i have created from the surface of the ground man along with animals creeping things and birds of the sky for i am sorry that i have made them
1 6 8 but noah found favor in yahweh s eyes
1 6 9 this is the history of the generations of noah noah was a righteous man blameless among the people of his time noah walked with god
1 6 10 noah became the father of three sons shem ham and japheth
1 6 11 the earth was corrupt before god and the earth was filled with violence
1 6 12 god saw the earth and saw that it was corrupt for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth
1 6 13 god said to noah i will bring an end to all flesh for the earth is filled with violence through them behold i will destroy them and the earth
1 6 14 make a ship of gopher wood you shall make rooms in the ship and shall seal it inside and outside with pitch
1 6 15 this is how you shall make it the length of the ship shall be three hundred cubits its width fifty cubits and its height thirty cubits
1 6 16 you shall make a roof in the ship and you shall finish it to a cubit upward you shall set the door of the ship in its side you shall make it with lower second and third levels
1 6 17 i even i do bring the flood of waters on this earth to destroy all flesh having the breath of life from under the sky everything that is in the earth will die
1 6 18 but i will establish my covenant with you you shall come into the ship you your sons your wife and your sons wives with you
1 6 19 of every living thing of all flesh you shall bring two of every sort into the ship to keep them alive with you they shall be male and female
1 6 20 of the birds after their kind of the livestock after their kind of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind two of every sort will come to you to keep them alive
1 6 21 take with you some of all food that is eaten and gather it to yourself and it will be for food for you and for them
1 6 22 thus noah did he did all that god commanded him
1 7 1 yahweh said to noah come with all of your household into the ship for i have seen your righteousness before me in this generation
1 7 2 you shall take seven pairs of every clean animal with you the male and his female of the animals that are not clean take two the male and his female
1 7 3 also of the birds of the sky seven and seven male and female to keep seed alive on the surface of all the earth
1 7 4 in seven days i will cause it to rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights i will destroy every living thing that i have made from the surface of the ground
1 7 5 noah did everything that yahweh commanded him
1 7 6 noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters came on the earth
1 7 7 noah went into the ship with his sons his wife and his sons wives because of the floodwaters
1 7 8 clean animals unclean animals birds and everything that creeps on the ground
1 7 9 went by pairs to noah into the ship male and female as god commanded noah
1 7 10 after the seven days the floodwaters came on the earth

1 7 11 in the six hundredth year of noah s life in the second month on the seventeenth day of the month on the same day all the fountains of the great deep were burst open and the sky s windows were opened
1 7 12 it rained on the earth forty days and forty nights
1 7 13 in the same day noah and shem ham and japheth the sons of noah and noah s wife and the three wives of his sons with them entered into the ship
1 7 14 they and every animal after its kind all the livestock after their kind every creeping thing that creeps on the earth after its kind and every bird after its kind every bird of every sort
1 7 15 pairs from all flesh with the breath of life in them went into the ship to noah
1 7 16 those who went in went in male and female of all flesh as god commanded him then yahweh shut him in
1 7 17 the flood was forty days on the earth the waters increased and lifted up the ship and it was lifted up above the earth
1 7 18 the waters rose and increased greatly on the earth and the ship floated on the surface of the waters
1 7 19 the waters rose very high on the earth all the high mountains that were under the whole sky were covered
1 7 20 the waters rose fifteen cubits higher and the mountains were covered
1 7 21 all flesh died that moved on the earth including birds livestock animals every creeping thing that creeps on the earth and every man
1 7 22 all on the dry land in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life died

1 7 23 every living thing was destroyed that was on the surface of the ground including man livestock creeping things and birds of the sky they were destroyed from the earth only noah was left and those who were with him in the ship
1 7 24 the waters flooded the earth one hundred fifty days
1 8 1 god remembered noah all the animals and all the livestock that were with him in the ship and god made a wind to pass over the earth the waters subsided
1 8 2 the deep s fountains and the sky s windows were also stopped and the rain from the sky was restrained
1 8 3 the waters continually receded from the earth after the end of one hundred fifty days the waters decreased
1 8 4 the ship rested in the seventh month on the seventeenth day of the month on ararat s mountains
1 8 5 the waters receded continually until the tenth month in the tenth month on the first day of the month the tops of the mountains were visible
1 8 6 at the end of forty days noah opened the window of the ship which he had made
1 8 7 and he sent out a raven it went back and forth until the waters were dried up from the earth
1 8 8 he himself sent out a dove to see if the waters were abated from the surface of the ground

1 8 9 but the dove found no place to rest her foot and she returned into the ship to him for the waters were on the surface of the whole earth he put out his hand and took her and brought her to him into the ship
1 8 10 he waited yet another seven days and again he sent the dove out of the ship
1 8 11 the dove came back to him at evening and behold in her mouth was a freshly plucked olive leaf so noah knew that the waters were abated from the earth
1 8 12 he waited yet another seven days and sent out the dove and she didn t return to him anymore

1 8 13 in the six hundred first year in the first month the first day of the month the waters were dried up from the earth noah removed the covering of the ship and looked he saw that the surface of the ground was dried
1 8 14 in the second month on the twenty seventh day of the month the earth was dry
1 8 15 god spoke to noah saying
1 8 16 go out of the ship you your wife your sons and your sons wives with you

1 8 17 bring out with you every living thing that is with you of all flesh including birds livestock and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth that they may breed abundantly in the earth and be fruitful and multiply on the earth
1 8 18 noah went out with his sons his wife and his sons wives with him
1 8 19 every animal every creeping thing and every bird whatever moves on the earth after their families went out of the ship
1 8 20 noah built an altar to yahweh and took of every clean animal and of every clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar

1 8 21 yahweh smelled the pleasant aroma yahweh said in his heart i will not again curse the ground any more for man s sake because the imagination of man s heart is evil from his youth i will never again strike every living thing as i have done
1 8 22 while the earth remains seed time and harvest and cold and heat and summer and winter and day and night will not cease
1 9 1 god blessed noah and his sons and said to them be fruitful multiply and replenish the earth

1 9 2 the fear of you and the dread of you will be on every animal of the earth and on every bird of the sky everything that moves along the ground and all the fish of the sea are delivered into your hand
1 9 3 every moving thing that lives will be food for you as i gave you the green herb i have given everything to you
1 9 4 but flesh with its life that is its blood you shall not eat
1 9 5 i will surely require your blood of your lives at the hand of every animal i will require it at the hand of man even at the hand of every man s brother i will require the life of man
1 9 6 whoever sheds man s blood his blood will be shed by man for god made man in his own image
1 9 7 be fruitful and multiply increase abundantly in the earth and multiply in it
1 9 8 god spoke to noah and to his sons with him saying
1 9 9 as for me behold i establish my covenant with you and with your offspring after you
1 9 10 and with every living creature that is with you the birds the livestock and every animal of the earth with you of all that go out of the ship even every animal of the earth
1 9 11 i will establish my covenant with you all flesh will not be cut off any more by the waters of the flood there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth
1 9 12 god said this is the token of the covenant which i make between me and you and every living creature that is with you for perpetual generations
1 9 13 i set my rainbow in the cloud and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth
1 9 14 when i bring a cloud over the earth that the rainbow will be seen in the cloud
1 9 15 and i will remember my covenant which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh and the waters will no more become a flood to destroy all flesh
1 9 16 the rainbow will be in the cloud i will look at it that i may remember the everlasting covenant between god and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth
1 9 17 god said to noah this is the token of the covenant which i have established between me and all flesh that is on the earth
1 9 18 the sons of noah who went out from the ship were shem ham and japheth ham is the father of canaan
1 9 19 these three were the sons of noah and from these the whole earth was populated
1 9 20 noah began to be a farmer and planted a vineyard
1 9 21 he drank of the wine and got drunk he was uncovered within his tent
1 9 22 ham the father of canaan saw the nakedness of his father and told his two brothers outside

1 9 23 shem and japheth took a garment and laid it on both their shoulders went in backwards and covered the nakedness of their father their faces were backwards and they didn t see their father s nakedness
1 9 24 noah awoke from his wine and knew what his youngest son had done to him
1 9 25 he said canaan is cursed he will be a servant of servants to his brothers
1 9 26 he said blessed be yahweh the god of shem let canaan be his servant
1 9 27 may god enlarge japheth let him dwell in the tents of shem let canaan be his servant
1 9 28 noah lived three hundred fifty years after the flood
1 9 29 all the days of noah were nine hundred fifty years and then he died
1 10 1 now this is the history of the generations of the sons of noah and of shem ham and japheth sons were born to them after the flood
1 10 2 the sons of japheth were gomer magog madai javan tubal meshech and tiras
1 10 3 the sons of gomer were ashkenaz riphath and togarmah
1 10 4 the sons of javan were elishah tarshish kittim and dodanim
1 10 5 of these were the islands of the nations divided in their lands everyone after his language after their families in their nations
1 10 6 the sons of ham were cush mizraim put and canaan
1 10 7 the sons of cush were seba havilah sabtah raamah and sabteca the sons of raamah were sheba and dedan
1 10 8 cush became the father of nimrod he began to be a mighty one in the earth
1 10 9 he was a mighty hunter before yahweh therefore it is said like nimrod a mighty hunter before yahweh
1 10 10 the beginning of his kingdom was babel erech accad and calneh in the land of shinar
1 10 11 out of that land he went into assyria and built nineveh rehoboth ir calah
1 10 12 and resen between nineveh and the great city calah
1 10 13 mizraim became the father of ludim anamim lehabim naphtuhim
1 10 14 pathrusim casluhim which the philistines descended from and caphtorim
1 10 15 canaan became the father of sidon his firstborn heth
1 10 16 the jebusites the amorites the girgashites
1 10 17 the hivites the arkites the sinites
1 10 18 the arvadites the zemarites and the hamathites afterward the families of the canaanites were spread abroad
1 10 19 the border of the canaanites was from sidon as you go toward gerar to gaza as you go toward sodom gomorrah admah and zeboiim to lasha
1 10 20 these are the sons of ham after their families according to their languages in their lands and their nations
1 10 21 children were also born to shem the father of all the children of eber the elder brother of japheth
1 10 22 the sons of shem were elam asshur arpachshad lud and aram
1 10 23 the sons of aram were uz hul gether and mash
1 10 24 arpachshad became the father of shelah shelah became the father of eber
1 10 25 to eber were born two sons the name of the one was peleg for in his days the earth was divided his brother s name was joktan
1 10 26 joktan became the father of almodad sheleph hazarmaveth jerah
1 10 27 hadoram uzal diklah
1 10 28 obal abimael sheba
1 10 29 ophir havilah and jobab all these were the sons of joktan
1 10 30 their dwelling extended from mesha as you go toward sephar the mountain of the east
1 10 31 these are the sons of shem by their families according to their languages lands and nations
1 10 32 these are the families of the sons of noah by their generations according to their nations the nations divided from these in the earth after the flood
1 11 1 the whole earth was of one language and of one speech
1 11 2 as they traveled east they found a plain in the land of shinar and they lived there
1 11 3 they said to one another come let s make bricks and burn them thoroughly they had brick for stone and they used tar for mortar
1 11 4 they said come let s build ourselves a city and a tower whose top reaches to the sky and let s make a name for ourselves lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole earth
1 11 5 yahweh came down to see the city and the tower which the children of men built
1 11 6 yahweh said behold they are one people and they have all one language and this is what they begin to do now nothing will be withheld from them which they intend to do
1 11 7 come let s go down and there confuse their language that they may not understand one another s speech
1 11 8 so yahweh scattered them abroad from there on the surface of all the earth they stopped building the city
1 11 9 therefore its name was called babel because there yahweh confused the language of all the earth from there yahweh scattered them abroad on the surface of all the earth
1 11 10 this is the history of the generations of shem shem was one hundred years old when he became the father of arpachshad two years after the flood
1 11 11 shem lived five hundred years after he became the father of arpachshad and became the father of more sons and daughters
1 11 12 arpachshad lived thirty five years and became the father of shelah

16 1 1 the words of nehemiah the son of hacaliah now in the month chislev in the twentieth year as i was in shushan the palace

16 1 5 and said i beg you yahweh the god of heaven the great and awesome god who keeps covenant and loving kindness with those who love him and keep his commandments

16 1 6 let your ear now be attentive and your eyes open that you may listen to the prayer of your servant which i pray before you at this time day and night for the children of israel your servants while i confess the sins of the children of israel which we have sinned against you yes i and my father s house have sinned

16 1 10 now these are your servants and your people whom you have redeemed by your great power and by your strong hand

16 2 1 in the month nisan in the twentieth year of artaxerxes the king when wine was before him i picked up the wine and gave it to the king now i had not been sad before in his presence
16 2 2 the king said to me why is your face sad since you are not sick this is nothing else but sorrow of heart then i was very much afraid
16 2 3 i said to the king let the king live forever why shouldn t my face be sad when the city the place of my fathers tombs lies waste and its gates have been consumed with fire
16 2 4 then the king said to me what is your request so i prayed to the god of heaven
16 2 5 i said to the king if it pleases the king and if your servant has found favor in your sight that you would send me to judah to the city of my fathers tombs that i may build it
16 2 6 the king said to me the queen was also sitting by him how long will your journey be when will you return so it pleased the king to send me and i set a time for he
16 2 7 moreover i said to the king if it pleases the king let letters be given me to the governors beyond the river that they may let me pass through until i come to judah

16 2 8 and a letter to asaph the keeper of the king s forest that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel by the temple for the wall of the city and for the house that i will occupy the king granted my requests because of the good hand of my god on me

16 2 11 so i came to jerusalem and was there three days

16 2 15 then went i up in the night by the brook and inspected the wall and i turned back and entered by the valley gate and so returned

16 2 17 then i said to them you see the bad situation that we are in how jerusalem lies waste and its gates are burned with fire come let us build up the wall of jerusalem that we won t be disgraced

17 1 1 now in the days of ahasuerus this is ahasuerus who reigned from india even to ethiopia over one hundred twenty seven provinces

26 1 1 now in the thirtieth year in the fourth month in the fifth of the month as i was among the captives by the river chebar the heavens were opened and i saw visions of god

26 1 4 i looked and behold a stormy wind came out of the north a great cloud with flashing lightning and a brightness around it and out of the middle of it as it were glowing metal out of the middle of the fire
26 1 5 out of its center came the likeness of four living creatures this was their appearance they had the likeness of a man
26 1 6 everyone had four faces and each one of them had four wings
26 1 7 their feet were straight feet and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf s foot and they sparkled like burnished brass
26 1 8 they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides and the four of them had their faces and their wings thus
26 1 9 their wings were joined to one another they didn t turn when they went each one went straight forward

26 1 10 as for the likeness of their faces they had the face of a man and the four of them had the face of a lion on the right side and the four of them had the face of an ox on the left side the four of them also had the face of an eagle
26 1 11 such were their faces their wings were spread out above two wings of each one touched another and two covered their bodies
26 1 12 each one went straight forward where the spirit was to go they went they didn t turn when they went

26 1 13 as for the likeness of the living creatures their appearance was like burning coals of fire like the appearance of torches the fire went up and down among the living creatures and the fire was bright and lightning went out of the fire
26 1 14 the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning

26 1 16 the appearance of the wheels and their work was like a beryl and the four of them had one likeness and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel within a wheel
26 1 17 when they went they went in their four directions they didn t turn when they went
26 1 18 as for their rims they were high and dreadful and the four of them had their rims full of eyes all around
26 1 19 when the living creatures went the wheels went beside them and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth the wheels were lifted up
26 1 20 wherever the spirit was to go they went there was the spirit to go and the wheels were lifted up beside them for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels

26 1 23 under the expanse were their wings straight the one toward the other each one had two which covered on this side and every one had two which covered on that side their bodies

26 1 24 when they went i heard the noise of their wings like the noise of great waters like the voice of the almighty a noise of tumult like the noise of an army when they stood they let down their wings

72 1 1 a copy of an epistle which jeremy sent to them which were to be led captives into babylon by the king of the babylonians to certify them as it was commanded him of god
72 1 2 because of the sins which you have committed before god you shall be led away captives to babylon by nabuchodonosor king of the babylonians
72 1 3 so when you come to babylon you shall remain there many years and for a long season even for seven generations and after that i will bring you out peaceably from thence
72 1 4 but now shall you see in babylon gods of silver and of gold and of wood borne upon shoulders which cause the nations to fear
72 1 5 beware therefore that you in no wise become like to the strangers neither let fear take hold upon you because of them when you see the multitude before them and behind them worshipping them
72 1 6 but say you in your hearts o lord we must worship you
72 1 7 for mine angel is with you and i myself do care for your souls
72 1 8 for their tongue is polished by the workman and they themselves are overlaid with gold and with silver yet are they but false and can t speak
72 1 9 and taking gold as it were for a virgin that loves to go gay they make crowns for the heads of their gods
72 1 10 and sometimes also the priests convey from their gods gold and silver and bestow it upon themselves
72 1 11 and will even give thereof to the common harlots and they deck them as men with garments even the gods of silver and gods of gold and of wood
72 1 12 yet can t these gods save themselves from rust and moths though they be covered with purple raiment
72 1 13 they wipe their faces because of the dust of the temple which is thick upon them
72 1 14 and he that can t put to death one that offends against him holds a sceptre as though he were judge of a country
72 1 15 he has also a dagger in his right hand and an axe but can t deliver himself from war and robbers
72 1 16 whereby they are known not to be gods therefore fear them not

72 1 17 for like as a vessel that a man uses is nothing worth when it is broken even so it is with their gods when they be set up in the temples their eyes be full of dust through the feet of them that come in

72 1 18 and as the courts are made sure on every side upon him that offends the king as being committed to suffer death even so the priests make fast their temples with doors with locks and bars lest they be carried off by robbers
72 1 19 they light them candles yes more than for themselves whereof they can t see one
72 1 20 they are as one of the beams of the temple and men say their hearts are eaten out when things creeping out of the earth devour both them and their raiment they feel it not
72 1 21 when their faces are blacked through the smoke that comes out of the temple
72 1 22 upon their bodies and heads alight bats swallows and birds and in like manner the cats also
72 1 23 whereby you may know that they are no gods therefore fear them not
72 1 24 notwithstanding the gold wherewith they are beset to make them beautiful except one wipe off the rust they will not shine for not even when they were molten did they feel it
72 1 25 things wherein there is no breath are bought at any cost
72 1 26 having no feet they are borne upon shoulders whereby they declare to men that they be nothing worth

72 1 27 they also that serve them are ashamed for if they fall to the ground at any time they can t rise up again of themselves neither if they be set awry can they make themselves straight but the offerings are set before them as if they were dead men

72 1 28 and the things that are sacrificed to them their priests sell and spend and in like manner their wives also lay up part thereof in salt but to the poor and to the impotent will they give nothing thereof
72 1 29 the menstruous woman and the woman in childbed touch their sacrifices knowing therefore by these things that they are no gods fear them not
72 1 30 for how can they be called gods because women set meat before the gods of silver gold and wood
72 1 31 and in their temples the priests sit on seats having their clothes tore and their heads and beards shaven and nothing upon their heads
72 1 32 they roar and cry before their gods as men do at the feast when one is dead
72 1 33 the priests also take off garments from them and clothe their wives and children withal
72 1 34 whether it be evil that one does to them or good they are not able to recompense it they can neither set up a king nor put him down
72 1 35 in like manner they can neither give riches nor money though a man make a vow to them and keep it not they will never exact it
72 1 36 they can save no man from death neither deliver the weak from the mighty
72 1 37 they can t restore a blind man to his sight nor deliver any that is in distress
72 1 38 they can show no mercy to the widow nor do good to the fatherless
72 1 39 they are like the stones that be hewn out of the mountain these gods of wood and that are overlaid with gold and with silver they that minister to them shall be confounded
72 1 40 how should a man then think or say that they are gods when even the chaldeans themselves dishonor them
72 1 41 who if they shall see one dumb that can t speak they bring him and entreat him to call upon bel as though he were able to understand
72 1 42 yet they can t perceive this themselves and forsake them for they have no understanding

72 1 43 the women also with cords about them sit in the ways burning bran for incense but if any of them drawn by some that passes by lie with him she reproaches her fellow that she was not thought as worthy as herself nor her cord broken
72 1 44 whatsoever is done among them is false how should a man then think or say that they are gods
72 1 45 they are fashioned by carpenters and goldsmiths they can be nothing else than the workmen will have them to be
72 1 46 and they themselves that fashioned them can never continue long how then should the things that are fashioned by them
72 1 47 for they have left lies and reproaches to them that come after
72 1 48 for when there comes any war or plague upon them the priests consult with themselves where they may be hidden with them
72 1 49 how then can t men understand that they be no gods which can neither save themselves from war nor from plague
72 1 50 for seeing they be but of wood and overlaid with gold and with silver it shall be known hereafter that they are false
72 1 51 and it shall be manifest to all nations and kings that they are no gods but the works of men s hands and that there is no work of god in them
72 1 52 who then may not know that they are no gods
72 1 53 for neither can they set up a king in a land nor give rain to men
72 1 54 neither can they judge their own cause nor redress a wrong being unable for they are as crows between heaven and earth
72 1 55 for even when fire falls upon the house of gods of wood or overlaid with gold or with silver their priests will flee away and escape but they themselves shall be burned asunder like beams
72 1 56 moreover they can t withstand any king or enemies how should a man then allow or think that they be gods
72 1 57 neither are those gods of wood and overlaid with silver or with gold able to escape either from thieves or robbers
72 1 58 whose gold and silver and garments wherewith they are clothed they that are strong will take from them and go away withal neither shall they be able to help themselves

72 1 59 therefore it is better to be a king that shows his manhood or else a vessel in a house profitable for that whereof the owner shall have need than such false gods or even a door in a house to keep the things safe that be therein than such false gods or a pillar of wood in a palace than such false gods
72 1 60 for sun and moon and stars being bright and sent to do their offices are obedient
72 1 61 likewise also the lightning when it glittereth is fair to see and after the same manner the wind also blows in every country
72 1 62 and when god commands the clouds to go over the whole world they do as they are bidden
72 1 63 and the fire sent from above to consume mountains and woods does as it is commanded but these are to be likened to them neither in show nor power
72 1 64 wherefore a man should neither think nor say that they are gods seeing they are able neither to judge causes nor to do good to men
72 1 65 knowing therefore that they are no gods fear them not
72 1 66 for they can neither curse nor bless kings
72 1 67 neither can they show signs in the heavens among the nations nor shine as the sun nor give light as the moon
72 1 68 the beasts are better than they for they can get under a covert and help themselves
72 1 69 in no wise then is it manifest to us that they are gods therefore fear them not
72 1 70 for as a scarecrow in a garden of cucumbers that keeps nothing so are their gods of wood and overlaid with gold and with silver

72 1 71 likewise also their gods of wood and overlaid with gold and with silver are like to a white thorn in an orchard that every bird sits upon as also to a dead body that is cast forth into the dark
72 1 72 and you shall know them to be no gods by the bright purple that rots upon them and they themselves afterward shall be consumed and shall be a reproach in the country
72 1 73 better therefore is the just man that has none idols for he shall be far from reproach
